# `silk/text/diff`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Line diffs, unified diff text, and reading and applying patches.

## When to use
Use [`unified`](#unified) to show how a file changed, as `diff -u` and `git diff` do, or to make a patch
that a later step applies. Use [`parse`](#parse) to read a patch from `diff -u`, `git diff`, or
`git format-patch`, and [`apply`](#apply) to apply one of its files to the original text. Use
[`diffLines`](#diffLines) or [`diffSymbols`](#diffSymbols) for the edits themselves, for example to show a side-by-side
view or to compare words instead of lines.

## Details
A line ends after each `\n`. A last line without `\n` is a line too, and it differs from the
same line with `\n`. Lines are compared byte for byte, so a `\r` before `\n` is part of the line.

The [`Algorithm`](#Algorithm) chooses how the shared lines are found:

- [`Algorithm.Histogram`](#Algorithm.Histogram) anchors the comparison on lines that are rare in both texts, as
  `git diff --histogram` does. It is the fastest, and the diffs are easy to read. Use it unless
  there is a reason to use another algorithm.
- [`Algorithm.MyersMinimal`](#Algorithm.MyersMinimal) always finds the fewest deleted and inserted lines, as
  `git diff --minimal` does. The time grows with the line count times the number of changed
  lines.
- [`Algorithm.Myers`](#Algorithm.Myers) stops a long search after about the square root of the line count, as
  `git diff` does by default, so very different texts do not take quadratic time. The diff can
  then have a few more changed lines than the minimum.

The edits are a list of [`Edit`](#Edit) runs. [`unified`](#unified) groups the changes into hunks with
`context` unchanged lines around them, and writes `\ No newline at end of file` after a last
line without `\n`, so the text reads back with [`parse`](#parse) and applies with [`apply`](#apply).

A [`Patch`](#Patch) holds one [`FilePatch`](#FilePatch) for each file. Its paths, hunks and lines are [`Span`](#Span)
ranges of the patch text, so the patch text must stay alive while the patch is in use.
[`apply`](#apply) puts each hunk where its old lines are, nearest to the line that the hunk header
gives, so a patch still applies after lines were added or removed before a hunk.

The `Bytes` forms, such as [`unifiedBytes`](#unifiedBytes), take and return bytes that need not be UTF-8, such
as file contents.

## Examples
### Make a patch and apply it
```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { Algorithm, ApplyError, FilePatch, PatchError }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! PatchError | ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let old = "red\ngreen\nblue\n"
  let new = "red\nyellow\nblue\n"
  let text = run diff.unified("a/colors.txt", old, "b/colors.txt", new, 3, Algorithm.Histogram)
  let expected = "--- a/colors.txt\n+++ b/colors.txt\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n red\n-green\n+yellow\n blue\n"
  if String.view(&text) != expected {
    return 1
  }
  let patch = run diff.parse(String.view(&text))
  let file = &List<FilePatch>.asSlice(&patch.files)[0]
  let patched = run diff.apply(old, String.view(&text), file)
  if String.view(&patched) != new {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: PatchError | ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `diff` with `import silk.text.diff as diff`.

<a id="Algorithm"></a>

## `Algorithm`

```silk
pub enum Algorithm
```

The algorithm that finds the lines two texts share.

### When to use

Use [`Algorithm.Histogram`](#Algorithm.Histogram) unless there is a reason to use another algorithm. It is the
fastest, and its diffs are easy to read.

### Details

All three algorithms give correct edits: applied to the old text, they give the new text. They
can differ in which lines they keep when more than one choice has the same cost, and
[`Algorithm.Myers`](#Algorithm.Myers) and [`Algorithm.Histogram`](#Algorithm.Histogram) can change a few more lines than the minimum.

<a id="Algorithm.Myers"></a>

### `Myers`

```silk
Myers
```

Myers' algorithm, as `git diff` uses by default. A search that takes longer than about the
square root of the line count stops at its best point so far, so the time stays low for very
different texts. The diff can then have a few more changed lines than the minimum.

<a id="Algorithm.MyersMinimal"></a>

### `MyersMinimal`

```silk
MyersMinimal
```

Myers' algorithm with no limit, as `git diff --minimal`. The diff has the fewest deleted and
inserted lines. The time grows with the line count times the number of changed lines.

<a id="Algorithm.Histogram"></a>

### `Histogram`

```silk
Histogram
```

The histogram algorithm, as `git diff --histogram`. It matches the lines that are rare in
both texts first, then the lines around them. It is the fastest of the three, and it keeps
rare lines, such as function headers, as anchors.

<a id="Edit"></a>

## `Edit`

```silk
pub struct Edit
```

One run of lines that are equal, deleted, or inserted.

### Details

The runs of a diff cover both sequences in order, with no gaps: each run starts where the last
one ended. An `Equal` run covers `length` lines of each sequence. A `Delete` run covers
`length` old lines and starts no new lines, and an `Insert` run covers `length` new lines and
starts no old lines. Where lines change, the `Delete` run comes before the `Insert` run. Line
indices start from 0.

```

```

<a id="diffSymbols"></a>

## `diffSymbols`

```silk
pub effect fn diffSymbols(old: &[u32], new: &[u32], algorithm: Algorithm) -> List<Edit>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the edits that turn the sequence `old` into `new`, where each number is one symbol.

### When to use

Use this function to compare sequences of things other than lines, such as words or tokens:
give equal things equal numbers, then compare the numbers. For lines of text, use
[`diffLines`](#diffLines).

### Details

The runs cover both sequences in order. Where symbols change, a `Delete` run comes before the
`Insert` run. The memory used grows with the sequence lengths and with the largest symbol, so
number the symbols from 0.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the scratch storage or the result.

### Examples

#### Compare two sequences of word numbers

```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { Algorithm, Edit, EditKind }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  // "the quick fox" against "the slow fox", one number per word.
  let old: [u32; 3] = [0, 1, 2]
  let new: [u32; 3] = [0, 3, 2]
  let edits = run diff.diffSymbols(&old, &new, Algorithm.Histogram)
  let runs = List<Edit>.asSlice(&edits)
  if runs.length != 4 || runs[1].kind != EditKind.Delete || runs[2].kind != EditKind.Insert {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn exhausted(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), exhausted) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="diffLines"></a>

## `diffLines`

```silk
pub effect fn diffLines(old: string, new: string, algorithm: Algorithm) -> List<Edit>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the edits that turn the lines of `old` into the lines of `new`.

### When to use

Use this function when the edits themselves are needed, for example to show a side-by-side
view or to count changed lines. Use [`unified`](#unified) for diff text.

### Details

A line ends after each `\n`. A last line without `\n` is a line too, and it differs from the
same line with `\n`. Lines are compared byte for byte. The runs cover both texts in order, with
line indices from 0. Where lines change, a `Delete` run comes before the `Insert` run.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the scratch storage or the result.

### Examples

#### Count the changed lines

```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { Algorithm, Edit, EditKind }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let edits = run diff.diffLines("a\nb\nc\n", "a\nc\nd\n", Algorithm.MyersMinimal)
  let runs = List<Edit>.asSlice(&edits)
  let mut deleted: usize = 0
  let mut inserted: usize = 0
  let mut at: usize = 0
  while at < runs.length {
    if runs[at].kind == EditKind.Delete {
      deleted = deleted + runs[at].length
    } else if runs[at].kind == EditKind.Insert {
      inserted = inserted + runs[at].length
    }
    at = at + 1
  }
  if deleted != 1 || inserted != 1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn exhausted(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), exhausted) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="unified"></a>

## `unified`

```silk
pub effect fn unified(
  oldName: string,
  old: string,
  newName: string,
  new: string,
  context: usize,
  algorithm: Algorithm,
) -> String
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the unified diff from `old` to `new`, with `context` unchanged lines around each change.

### When to use

Use this function to show how a text changed, or to make a patch for [`apply`](#apply) or for tools
such as `patch` and `git apply`.

### Details

The diff starts with `--- oldName` and `+++ newName`, then has one `@@ -start,count +start,count
@@` hunk for each group of changes. Changes with at most `2 * context` unchanged lines between
them share a hunk. Each line starts with `' '` for an unchanged line, `'-'` for a deleted line,
or `'+'` for an inserted line. A last line without `\n` is followed by `\n\ No newline at end
of file\n`. The names are written as given, so pass `a/path` and `b/path` for the form that
`git apply` expects. The usual `context` is 3.

Equal texts give an empty diff, with no header.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the scratch storage or the result.

### Gotchas

A name that contains a tab or a newline makes a header that other tools read differently.

### Examples

#### Write a diff with one line of context

```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { Algorithm }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let old = "one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\n"
  let new = "one\n2\nthree\nfour"
  let text = run diff.unified("a/n.txt", old, "b/n.txt", new, 1, Algorithm.Histogram)
  let expected = "--- a/n.txt\n+++ b/n.txt\n@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@\n one\n-two\n+2\n three\n-four\n+four\n\\ No newline at end of file\n"
  if String.view(&text) != expected {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn exhausted(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), exhausted) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

`source` must be the text that the span came from. The function traps if the span ends

<a id="Hunk"></a>

## `Hunk`

```silk
pub struct Hunk
```

One hunk of a file patch: its `@@` header and where its lines are.

### Details

The numbers are as the header gives them. A range with no lines, such as `-0,0`, gives the line
before the change, so its start is one less than for a range with lines. The lines of the hunk
are `lineCount` items of [`FilePatch.lines`](#FilePatch.lines) from `firstLine`.

<a id="FilePatch"></a>

## `FilePatch`

```silk
pub struct FilePatch
```

The changes to one file: its paths, modes, and hunks.

### Details

The paths and lines are [`Span`](#Span) ranges of the patch text. In a git patch, the paths lose their
`a/` and `b/` prefixes, so they are relative to the repository. In other patches they are as
written in the `---` and `+++` lines, up to a tab. Use [`apply`](#apply) to apply the hunks to the old
text.

<a id="ApplyError"></a>

## `ApplyError`

```silk
pub struct ApplyError
```

The error from [`apply`](#apply) or [`applyBytes`](#applyBytes): a hunk whose old lines are not in the original.

<a id="parse"></a>

## `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(text: string) -> Patch
  ! PatchError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads the patch `text`, as `diff -u`, `git diff`, and `git format-patch` write it.

### When to use

Use this function to read a patch before [`apply`](#apply) applies its files, or to list the files and
changes that a patch makes.

### Details

A file starts at a `diff --git` line, or at a `---` line that a `+++` line follows. Git
extended header lines give the modes, renames, copies, and binary changes. Each hunk reads as
many lines as its `@@` header gives, and a `\ No newline at end of file` line removes the `\n`
of the line before it. Other lines, such as a commit message or `index` lines, are skipped.
The parts of the result are [`Span`](#Span) ranges of `text`.

### Errors

- `PatchError` with reason `InvalidHunkHeader` for an `@@` line that is not a hunk header,
  `InvalidHunkLine` for a hunk line that does not start with `' '`, `'-'`, `'+'`, or `'\\'` or
  that is more than the header gives, `UnexpectedEnd` if the text ends in a hunk,
  `MissingFileHeader` for a hunk before any file header, and `InvalidMode` for a mode that is
  not octal.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.

### Gotchas

Quoted git paths, which git writes for names with special characters, keep their quotes and
escapes.

### Examples

#### List the files of a git patch

```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { FileChange, FilePatch, PatchError, Span }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! PatchError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let text = "diff --git a/src/app.js b/src/app.js\nindex 1111111..2222222 100644\n--- a/src/app.js\n+++ b/src/app.js\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-let x = 1\n+let x = 2\ndiff --git a/notes.txt b/notes.txt\nnew file mode 100644\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/notes.txt\n@@ -0,0 +1 @@\n+hello\n"
  let patch = run diff.parse(text)
  let files = List<FilePatch>.asSlice(&patch.files)
  if files.length != 2 || files[1].change != FileChange.Created {
    return 1
  }
  let path = match files[0].newPath {
    Option<Span>.Some {value} => value.text(text)
    Option<Span>.None => ""
  }
  if path != "src/app.js" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: PatchError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="parseBytes"></a>

## `parseBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn parseBytes(text: &[u8]) -> Patch
  ! PatchError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads the patch `text`, given as bytes that need not be UTF-8, as `diff -u`, `git diff`, and
`git format-patch` write it.

### When to use

Use this function for a patch read from a file, whose contents need not be UTF-8. For text, use
[`parse`](#parse).

### Details

A file starts at a `diff --git` line, or at a `---` line that a `+++` line follows. Git
extended header lines give the modes, renames, copies, and binary changes. Each hunk reads as
many lines as its `@@` header gives, and a `\ No newline at end of file` line removes the `\n`
of the line before it. Other lines are skipped. The parts of the result are [`Span`](#Span) ranges of
`text`.

### Errors

- `PatchError` with reason `InvalidHunkHeader`, `InvalidHunkLine`, `UnexpectedEnd`,
  `MissingFileHeader`, or `InvalidMode`, and the line number of the problem.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.

<a id="apply"></a>

## `apply`

```silk
pub effect fn apply(original: string, patch: string, file: &FilePatch) -> String
  ! ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `original` with the hunks of `file` applied, where `file` was read from `patch`.

### When to use

Use this function to apply one file of a patch that [`parse`](#parse) read, for example to patch a
dependency before a build.

### Details

The hunks apply in order. Each hunk goes where its context and deleted lines are the lines of
`original`, first at the line that its header gives, adjusted by how far the last hunk moved,
then at the nearest line before or after that place. Lines are compared byte for byte,
including the `\n`. A new file applies to an empty `original`. Only the hunks change the text:
renames, modes, and binary changes are for the caller to make.

### Errors

- `ApplyError` with the index of the first hunk whose old lines are not in `original` after the
  last applied hunk.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.

### Gotchas

`patch` must be the text that `file` was read from, because the lines of `file` are ranges of
it.

### Examples

#### Apply a hunk after the file grew

```silk
import silk.text.diff
import silk.text.diff { ApplyError, FilePatch, PatchError }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! PatchError | ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let text = "--- a/list.txt\n+++ b/list.txt\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n apple\n-banana\n+cherry\n melon\n"
  let patch = run diff.parse(text)
  let file = &List<FilePatch>.asSlice(&patch.files)[0]
  let patched = run diff.apply("fig\napple\nbanana\nmelon\n", text, file)
  if String.view(&patched) != "fig\napple\ncherry\nmelon\n" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: PatchError | ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="applyBytes"></a>

## `applyBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn applyBytes(original: &[u8], patch: &[u8], file: &FilePatch) -> Bytes
  ! ApplyError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the bytes `original` with the hunks of `file` applied, where `file` was read from the
bytes `patch`.

### When to use

Use this function for file contents that need not be UTF-8. For text, use [`apply`](#apply).

### Details

The hunks apply in order. Each hunk goes where its context and deleted lines are the lines of
`original`, first at the line that its header gives, adjusted by how far the last hunk moved,
then at the nearest line before or after that place. Lines are compared byte for byte,
including the `\n`. Only the hunks change the bytes: renames, modes, and binary changes are for
the caller to make.

### Errors

- `ApplyError` with the index of the first hunk whose old lines are not in `original` after the
  last applied hunk.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the result.

### Gotchas

`patch` must be the bytes that `file` was read from, because the lines of `file` are ranges of
them.
